definitions.explanation: A word of native Japanese origin, as opposed to words borrowed from Chinese (漢語) or other languages (外来語). Also called 大和言葉 (yamato kotoba).

examples.japanese: {和語|わご}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{漢語|かんご}→漢語：13439_kango⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{比|くら}べて→比べる：01237_kuraberu⟧⟦{柔|やわ}らかい→柔らかい：01096_yawarakai⟧⟦{響|ひび}き→響き：00098_hibiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Native Japanese words have a softer sound compared to Sino-Japanese words.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{語彙|ごい}→語彙：14214_goi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{和語|わご}、⟦{漢語|かんご}→漢語：13439_kango⟧、⟦{外来語|がいらいご}→外来語：12101_gairaigo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{三|みっ}つ→三つ：02970_mittsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{大|おお}きく→大きい：00335_ookii⟧⟦{分|わ}けられ→分ける：02333_wakeru⟧、⟦それぞれ→それぞれ：01453_sorezore⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{異|こと}なる→異なる：02101_kotonaru⟧⟦{特徴|とくちょう}→特徴：03456_tokuchou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っている→持つ：00478_motsu⟧。
examples.english: Japanese vocabulary is broadly divided into three categories — native words, Sino-Japanese words, and loanwords — each with distinct characteristics.

notes:
USAGE:
A linguistic term used when discussing the origins and layers of Japanese vocabulary. Japanese vocabulary is traditionally classified into three categories: {和語|わご} (native Japanese), ⟦{漢語|かんご}→漢語：13439_kango⟧ (Sino-Japanese, borrowed from Chinese), and ⟦{外来語|がいらいご}→外来語：12101_gairaigo⟧ (loanwords from other languages). {和語|わご} is also called ⟦{大和言葉|やまとことば}→大和言葉：14853_yamatokotoba⟧.

KEY CHARACTERISTICS:
{和語|わご} tends to sound softer and more emotional than ⟦{漢語|かんご}→漢語：13439_kango⟧. Many basic, everyday words are {和語|わご}: ⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ (to eat), ⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧ (to walk), ⟦{美|うつく}しい→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧ (beautiful). Kanji used for {和語|わご} are read with ⟦{訓読|くんよ}み→訓読み：10454_kunyomi⟧ (native readings).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {和語|わご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{読|よ}み→読み：00425_yomi⟧: native Japanese reading
- {和語|わご}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{漢語|かんご}→漢語：13439_kango⟧: native and Sino-Japanese words
- ⟦{大和言葉|やまとことば}→大和言葉：14853_yamatokotoba⟧: yamato kotoba (synonym)
